participants: Setter, labelled 'Speaker 1' — named in the file title as Kim Forbes-Sobers; he books calls, texts leads, writes CRM notes and reports his daily dial/set count
summary: Fourteen-minute closer-and-setter pipeline sync, the second in this batch between the same pair. Richard debriefs a call with a prospect transcribed as 'Montana' that went nowhere: the man's back is 'blown out', he was in bed and off camera, he has a personal-training background and was only looking around, so Richard gave pricing clarity, never pitched, and booked a second call for Thursday. The setter accepts he did not screen the injury. They then run the next two days' calendar, chase unresponsive leads, discuss how they estimate prospects' incomes, and Richard talks through his month-to-date cash position and his frustration that he is taking deposits while another closer takes $6,000 paid in full.
notable: No clinical screening exists at the setting stage and the setter says so plainly about a prospect with an acute back injury: 'I don't actually think I asked many questions about whether he's actually good to start training now. So that's funny on me.' The setter had already confirmed the prospect to 'three to four weekly sessions... 30 to 45 minutes each' while he was in bed with the injury; the closer's response was 'the injured part is a little bit of a red flag, of course', and a second call was booked anyway.

Income qualification is being done with ChatGPT. Of a commercial diver: 'when I put that into ChatGPT, it said he was probably making around, 75k, around there.' Of the 23-year-old firefighter: 'I once again chat GPT'd, like, estimated salary for, like, a five-year-old firefighter, and it said that would be around 60k.' These estimates are then written into CRM notes as qualification.

$100 deposits are being taken as a systematic close, not a one-off: 'those two that I did at down payment earlier today', 'Why would a sales guy do a deposit of 100 just to get rid of me?', and the contrast the closer draws — 'the Andrew is closing 6K [paid in full] and I'm just getting down payments and whatever. annoying.'

The closer is under explicit personal cash pressure and ties it directly to how he intends to sell: 'I want to get to the 50K, and that means I have to do another 24K, my projection is 22, and I'm only at 12 so far'; 'that's also the only reason I open my Friday, just need to get the cash in for myself, but also for the team'; and of the injured 23-year-old firefighter, 'I will do my best to sell him on something. It's just, it's annoying because I need to get the cash.'

A lead the setter believed was low intent was booked deliberately anyway: 'this is one of those guys who I knew had the money, but I financially qualified. I had him regardless, just like, because I almost wanted him to DQ himself, he was that low-intent.'

Availability is triaged by expected wallet size: 'if someone is a commercial diver, I think they do make money'; 'I'll sort of screw up my sleep for one day, but uh with someone that's like mid intense don't even do it please.'

Non-response to an introduction text is treated as a disqualifying signal: 'when someone doesn't respond to me, I'm like, why don't you respond to me? Because literally I've introduced myself. That's like the first red flag that I have.'
Transcript quality: overlapping speech merges turns at 00:05:31 and 00:09:32; the prospect name appears as both 'Montana' and 'Discord' and is almost certainly a mis-transcription of one name.
